findings.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — The second `downsize` definition overrides the existing five-argument method, so any caller using `downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` now raises `ArgumentError`.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Replacing the type-specific configured limit with 10 MB makes attachments and images above an administrator's lower configured limit pass client validation, even though only images are subsequently downsized.
app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — The new iterative downsizing path has no tests for successful reduction, no-progress failures, or the five-attempt cap.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: the hardcoded 10MB (10 * 1024 KB) limit replaces the type-specific configured limit from SiteSettings, causing client-side validation to diverge from server-side/administrator-configured limits. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — The new iterative downsizing path has no tests for successful reduction, no-progress failures, or the five-attempt cap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new iterative downsizing logic at lines 63-69 in uploads_controller.rb that attempts to reduce image size up to 5 times. This is non-trivial logic with specific edge cases (successful reduction, images that can't be reduced further, hitting the 5-attempt cap). The finding correctly identifies that this new functionality lacks test coverage. The diff shows no test files being modified, and this is substantive new behavior that warrants testing.
